title: Onprem module upgrade sidecar patterns
content:
Context and problem statement:

We need a repeatable, low-risk strategy for rolling forward breaking changes to Terraform primitives used by private deployments (VPC, IAM, EKS/GKE/AKS). Historically we see: consumers pinning outputs, downstream modules relying on implicit fields, and ops teams blocked by stateful migrations. This note sketches a conservative pattern we can apply across on-prem/VPC modules to enable canary upgrades, automated compatibility, and clearer deprecation paths.

Goals (ranked):
- avoid manual state surgery for customers
- enable canary upgrades and percentage-based rollouts for private clusters
- keep module interfaces explicit and discoverable
- provide automated compatibility shims to reduce breakage surface
- make deprecation visible in CI/plan output and console dashboards

Core pattern: upgrade-sidecar module + facade outputs

Idea in one line: ship a tiny "compatibility sidecar" alongside a new module version that maps old outputs and variable shapes to the new internal representation. Consumers can continue to read stable output names while we migrate real resources behind the facade.

What the sidecar does:
- provides outputs with legacy names (legacy_vpc_id, legacy_eks_cluster_name) that read from new resources or from data sources pointed at the previous resources if present
- implements explicit deprecation signals via an output e.g. deprecation_notice and a boolean legacy_mode_enabled variable
- includes a runtime validation data source that fails plan/apply in CI for known incompatible combinations (opt-in in prod)

Pattern components (module-level):
- module root: new implementation (v2+) that owns live resources and new-named outputs
- compatibility_sidecar submodule: optional, invoked by the root when var.enable_compat_sidecar == true
- facade outputs: stable names documented in module README under "compatibility layer"
- sentinel outputs: module exposes module_stability_tag and module_compatibility_level string outputs

Variable & output naming conventions:
- variables: use snake_case with explicit purpose, avoid "name" generic vars when representing multiple things (vpc_name -> controller_vpc_name if it controls cluster creation)
- feature flags: enable_compat_sidecar (bool), compat_mode_grace_period_days (number), compat_warn_only (bool)
- new outputs: v2_vpc_id, v2_eks_cluster_arn, v2_subnet_ids
- legacy outputs: vpc_id, eks_cluster_name, subnet_ids (present via sidecar)

Versioning and compatibility metadata:
- semantic versioning for modules (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) + a stability tag output (module_stability_tag) exposed to consumers
- compatibility_level defined as: 0 = breaking, 1 = additive, 2 = fully backward-compatible shim available

Upgrade strategy (consumer-facing runbook):
1) Read module_stability_tag and compatibility_level from current module version. If compatibility_level < 2, plan for canary.
2) Create a branch using new module version and set var.enable_compat_sidecar = true and var.compat_warn_only = true. Run terraform plan in CI and inspect deprecation_notice output.
3) For onprem clusters: run canary on a noncritical cluster or a single namespace via node pool labeling and instance group mapping.
4) After 1–2 weeks of telemetry, flip compat_warn_only = false to surface hard validation failures in plans in staging.
5) At 50% traffic/usage, disable sidecar and switch consumers to new outputs, then remove sidecar in next minor release.

State migration approaches (no manual state edits when possible):
- data bridge: a data source that looks up existing resources and constructs new ones (preferred when provider allows)
- shadow resource approach: create new resources and migrate traffic incrementally (used for EKS nodegroups, LB attachments)
- state-import helper script (last resort): documented script that imports a resource into new模块 state; must run in maintenance window and is logged

Contract-testing and CI requirements:
- add a module_consumer_test job that performs: init + plan against a small mocked account, asserting that legacy outputs exist when enable_compat_sidecar=true
- smoke test that applies a minimal example (dry-run) in ephemeral env via our internal infra-lab runner
- add a regression eval for common consumer patterns (e.g., kube_auth mapping, nodegroup tag propagation)

Operational signals to expose in Console/Runbooks:
- module_stability_tag and deprecation_notice as top-level fields displayed in console route when a customer uses a private-deploy module version older than N days
- cost/latency impact note when using sidecar (some extra data lookups may be performed)

Examples (pseudo-terraform snippets):

# consumer usage (minimal)
module "vpc" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//vpc?ref=v2.1.0"
  enable_compat_sidecar = true
  compat_warn_only = true
}

# sidecar outputs exposed to consumers
output "vpc_id" {
  value = module.compatibility_sidecar.legacy_vpc_id
  description = "Legacy stable output for consumer modules (deprecated, mapped to v2_vpc_id)"
}

Decision log (short):
- Considered: rename outputs with migration window (no shim). Rejected: too many breakages for private customers with strict change windows.
- Considered: automatically maintain both old and new resources. Rejected: cost and surface area for onprem air-gapped customers.
- Chosen: compatibility sidecar + deprecation signals, with opt-in and clear runbook for controlled migration.

Open questions / TODOs:
- policy: what is the default grace period we enforce before we start requiring compatibility shims? (30d vs 90d)
- infra-lab: add a test harness for import scenarios (EKS cluster import) and capture exact steps for each cloud variant
- automation: can we add a module-tooling utility to generate sidecar scaffolding for any module?
- docs: add a consumer-facing migration checklist and sample PR template for infra teams

Quick checklist for module authors (PR template):
- bump module version and add CHANGELOG entry
- add module_stability_tag and compatibility_level outputs
- add compat sidecar submodule and tests
- update README with migration steps and example consumer snippet
- run module_consumer_test in CI and attach results to PR

Notes to self / rough experiment log:
- tested a prototype for EKS: sidecar read of aws_eks_cluster.cluster[0].endpoint worked when using data "aws_eks_cluster" (import-free), but nodegroup migration still required planned replacements in our lab due to IAM role name collisions (INFRA-742 follow-up).
- found that some customers rely on implicit subnet ordering; add explicit output for subnet_roles = [private, public] instead of indexing subnet_ids[0].

References and links: JIRA-INFRA-742 (migration blockers), confluence page for Module Upgrade Playbook, PR example in terraform-modules repo.

If this pattern looks ok, next actions: 1) prototype sidecar scaffold generator, 2) land one pilot module (vpc) with sidecar and observe upgrades for 4 weeks, 3) codify CI checks into org-wide module template.

-- Monica
